description:
Project: In-console usage insights (cost drivers by route)

Goal
- Add first-class, in-console “usage insights” that attribute cost and latency to developer-defined routes/endpoints and to model variants.
- Help customers quickly answer: “What routes are costing us the most?”, “Which models drive spend on those routes?”, and “What changed week-over-week?”
- Provide exportable reports (CSV + JSON) suitable for finance/ops workflows and for attaching to internal incident/cost reviews.

Scope (what ships)
- New dimensions in the telemetry pipeline: `route` (developer-supplied or gateway-derived), `model`, and key request attributes needed for “top drivers” views.
- Aggregations and APIs to power console dashboards:
  - Cost: total, input/output tokens, cached tokens, GPU time proxy (if available), and unit cost.
  - Performance: p50/p95 latency and error rates by route/model.
  - “Top cost drivers” breakdowns with filters (time range, environment, region, org/project, deployment mode).
- Console UI:
  - Route list with spend ranking, sparklines, and quick filters.
  - Route detail view with model breakdown and “what changed” deltas.
  - Export action generating a bounded report with audit logging.
- Docs & DevEx updates:
  - How to set route identifiers across SDKs / gateway.
  - Best practices for cardinality control and naming conventions.

Non-goals (explicitly out of scope for initial GA)
- Full cost anomaly detection/alerting (beyond basic “change vs prior period” UI).
- Customer-configurable custom dimensions beyond route/model.
- Long-term historical exports beyond retention policy.

Key stakeholders / teams
- Product (Console & Rollouts): Marissa Cole (Dir), Paula Mendes (PM)
- Design: Tessa Morgan
- Engineering (Telemetry & Analytics Platform): Logan Wright (EM), Nadia Rahman, Caleb Johnson, Mei Lin
- SRE/Observability: Allison Grant
- DevEx: Alex Martinez (VP), Monica Patel (SDK), Elliot Price / Wei Chen (Docs)
- Security/Compliance: review for export auditing + RBAC considerations

Constraints / risks
- Cardinality: route naming can explode metric dimensions; must enforce limits, hashing/rollups, and guidance.
- Accuracy vs freshness: near-real-time dashboarding vs delayed, more accurate cost attribution (e.g., late-arriving token metering).
- RBAC & data exposure: exports must respect org/project boundaries and be auditable.
- Backfill: introducing new dimensions requires backfill strategy (or explicit “available after” messaging).

Timeline (hypothetical)
- Phase 0 (Week 1): kickoff, PRD, design explorations, telemetry/data model decisions.
- Phase 1 (Weeks 2–4): pipeline + aggregation + API MVP (route + model breakdown), initial console UI.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 5–6): export reports, RBAC/audit logging, backfill tooling, performance hardening.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 7–8): beta with design partners, docs/SDK updates, GA launch + release notes.

Deliverables
- Confluence PRD + design spec + ADRs
- Linear project with sequenced issues and dependencies
- GitHub PR set across `redwood` (console + services), `observability-pack`, `redwood-docs`, and a small SDK/quickstart touch
- Drive working docs (mockups, dataset schema sheets, launch brief)
- Slack coordination threads across product/eng/devex/support
- Support readiness artifacts (Jira known-issue patterns)
- Optional GTM artifacts: HubSpot notes + Fireflies calls that motivate export/reporting requirements

files.description: PRD: problem statement, target users (eng + ops), route/model breakdown requirements, export requirements, success metrics, rollout plan, and non-goals.
Design spec: information architecture, dashboards/views, filter model, empty states, pagination/limits, and accessibility notes for route + model cost drivers.
ADR: canonical definition of `route` (SDK-provided vs gateway-derived), normalization rules, length limits, allowed characters, and migration/backward compatibility.
Standards: cardinality budgets, sampling/rollups, recommended naming conventions for routes, and warnings for dynamic route IDs (e.g., user IDs).
API standards/addendum: endpoint shapes for route/model aggregations, pagination, time windows, and export job API; includes error codes and rate limits.
Security spec: audit log events for report export/download (who/when/filters), retention, and required fields for compliance evidence.
Operational dashboards: pipeline lag, aggregation job latency, export job success rates, API p95s, and cardinality alarms.
Runbook: how to backfill new dimensions, recompute aggregates, validate correctness, and safely roll back; includes commands and guardrails.
SLO doc: freshness and availability targets for insights APIs (e.g., data latency), error budget policy, and alert thresholds.
Support-facing known issues: why route costs may not match invoices exactly, late data arrival, missing route tags, and common mitigations.
DevEx plan: docs changes, SDK guidance, quickstart snippets, and the minimal examples required to teach route tagging + exporting reports.
Release notes draft: feature summary, limitations, required customer actions (route tagging), and links to docs.
Informal engineering doc: early decisions, open questions, edge cases (multi-model fallback), and links to relevant Linear issues/PRs.
Sheet-style doc: proposed tables/columns for aggregates, partitioning strategy, and example queries powering top-cost drivers.
Slides: UI mock explorations (table vs treemap, route detail view), pros/cons, and design feedback notes.
Draft API contract doc: request/response examples for route list, route detail, model breakdown, and export job creation.
Draft DevEx guidance: how to set route identifiers in Python/TS/Go, naming conventions, and examples for common frameworks.
Launch brief: target audiences, beta plan, GA checklist, comms plan, and internal enablement needs.
Sheet: beta customer feedback by account, requested filters/exports, severity, and status/owner.
Checklist: pre-launch monitoring (pipeline lag, API error rates), feature flag gates, and rollback triggers.
Short exec update: progress, risks (cardinality/export), resourcing asks, and expected ship date.
PDF-style note: benchmark results for export generation (CSV size limits, timeouts), and recommended guardrails.
PM umbrella issue: define success metrics, scope, and milestones for “In-console usage insights”; links to PRD/design spec.
Design task: route list + route detail information architecture; includes acceptance criteria for filters, empty states, and export placement.
Engineering epic: telemetry pipeline changes to emit/ingest route dimension; includes risks and cardinality mitigation plan.
Backend: build aggregates for cost by route/model (daily + hourly windows), with retention and partitioning details.
Backend API: route list endpoint (top spend, filters, pagination) with SLA targets and query cost budget.
Backend API: route detail endpoint with model breakdown, deltas vs prior period, and caching strategy.
Export: implement export job creation + download flow; define max rows, file formats, and audit events.
Console UI: route insights table + filters; includes performance requirements and loading states.
Console UI: route detail page with model breakdown chart/table; includes definition of cost metrics shown.
RBAC: ensure insights respect org/project scoping; tests for cross-project leakage; coordinate with security review.
Backfill tooling: one-time recompute for aggregates post-launch; includes safety checks and validation queries.
Observability: add dashboards/alerts for pipeline lag + export failures; includes alert thresholds and runbook links.
Docs: update docs site with route tagging and usage insights export guide; coordinate with DevEx writers.
SDKs: add/standardize route tagging helper (or header) across SDKs; include example snippets and tests.
Beta program: select design partners, define beta entry criteria, feedback cadence, and GA gating checklist.
Performance work: query optimization and caching for top routes view; load testing plan and acceptance thresholds.
Privacy/retention review: confirm export retention and data residency behavior; coordinate with Security & Compliance.
Instrumentation: ensure model fallback/routing events still attribute cost to the original route; edge-case test plan.
PR: Add route dimension plumbed through request context and metering events; includes migration notes and tests.
PR: Create aggregate tables/materialized views for cost by route/model; includes partitioning and backfill script.
PR: Implement insights API endpoint for top routes; includes pagination, filter parsing, and query cost limits.
PR: Implement route detail API (model breakdown + deltas); adds caching and response schema validation.
PR: Console UI route insights page (table, filters, basic charts); includes screenshots and feature flag.
PR: Console UI route detail view (model breakdown component, compare to prior period); includes UX review feedback.
PR: Export job service + download endpoint; adds CSV/JSON formatting, size limits, and retry logic.
PR: Audit logging for export actions + RBAC checks for insights endpoints; includes security review checklist.
PR: Add pipeline lag metrics + export job metrics; includes dashboards links and alert rule stubs.
PR: Add Grafana dashboards for usage-insights pipeline health and API p95; includes alert suggestions.
PR: Docs page for route tagging + usage insights overview; includes screenshots and FAQ about cost mismatch.
PR: Export reports documentation (CSV schema, limits, audit logging behavior) and troubleshooting section.
PR: Add `route` option to client request helpers (or standardized header); includes examples and unit tests.
PR: Add route tagging support + docsstring examples; ensure compatibility with streaming APIs.
